title: Collection adapter
description: An owner-registered adapter record (design section 6, Execution authorization). Registering one is CLI-only. The checked-in manifest and any submitted payload can select declarations and tests; they can never replace the executable, add shell fragments, change the root or install a runner.

grammar.description: Pins the argv shape. The selectors are data; the grammar is code.

executable.description: Absolute path; the identity of the executable is part of the record.

entry.description: Manifest directory (cargo) or package directory (vitest), relative to workspaceRoot.

tsconfig.description: vitest-run/1 only (F5): the tsconfig the collection typechecks against, relative to the package directory (workspaceRoot/entry), no `..` segment, an existing file. Default tsconfig.json. A file that extends the repository's own and lists only what the instrumentation imports keeps unrelated type errors from blocking a collect.

vitestConfig.description: vitest-run/1 only (F5): the vitest config the run uses (it lists the paneweft reporter), relative to the package directory, no `..` segment, an existing file. Default vitest.config.ts.

limitCeilings.description: Operator ceilings for the capture bounds a collect request may ask for (S3). A request can only lower a bound; it is clamped to the smaller of these and the SDK defaults. Absent: the SDK defaults are the ceiling.

env.description: The environment of every job of this adapter (F21). A job gets qex's minimal environment (HOME, LANG, LOGNAME, PATH, SHELL, USER of the submitting process), then the names in `passthrough` that the submitting process has (a list the host adds to: RUSTUP_HOME, CARGO_HOME, RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN, CARGO_TARGET_DIR, TMPDIR, LC_ALL, TERM, SSL_CERT_FILE, SSL_CERT_DIR), then `set`, which wins. Values in `set` do not depend on who submits, so a CLI call and an MCP call run the same job; a passthrough name does.
